A short pair of concentric rings stays near the hands. Keep the face, complete body and both shoes visible without duplicated silhouettes or musical-note lettering.
Use the supplied accepted anime reference to preserve the recognizable face, natural body build, hairstyle, clothing, accessories and palette. Redraw that same original person with the stronger angular ink, sculpted cel shadows and powerful 1990s battle-anime posing described above. Produce a SINGLE square 3 by 3 sprite sheet, exactly 9 equally sized invisible cells in a uniform mathematical grid. Read left to right, then top to bottom. One COMPLETE full-body pose per cell, including BOTH shoes. All poses face RIGHT: the nose, chest, leading fist and attacking foot point toward the right edge; especially the sweep, airkick and punches attack RIGHT. Consistent side-on camera and body scale across all nine cells. Choose a small enough body scale that the widest kick and longest horizontal down pose fit their own cells. Each standing figure is approximately 60% of its cell height, with shoes at 82% of cell height and the head near 22%. Center each whole pose inside its cell, including horizontal and airborne poses. Every hand, shoe, hair tip, accessory and attached energy accent stays within the central 76% of its cell, with at least 12% clear green on ALL four sides. The bottom row, including entrance, must show both complete feet and clear green below them. No limb crosses a cell boundary. Every complete silhouette is separated from its neighbors by uninterrupted green corridors: keep horizontal canvas bands from 30% to 37% and from 63% to 70% entirely empty green. Keep matching vertical green corridors between the three columns. No shoe touches another pose's hair, hand or effects. Keep special energy compact and attached to the palms, without a long beam reaching a cell edge; the game supplies the traveling projectile. No cropping at the outer canvas edge. Cell divisions are completely invisible: NO grid lines, panels, frames, dividers, gutters in another color, numbers or labels. Avoid large aura clouds on sprites; use compact attached energy accents only. These are named key poses, not a smooth nine-frame loop.
Cell 1 (row 1, column 1): punchwind - lead-hand jab chambered at the shoulder, about to strike right.
Cell 2 (row 1, column 2): kickwind - front knee raised and chambered before a kick to the right.
Cell 3 (row 1, column 3): heavywind - rear arm pulled far back, torso coiled for a heavy blow.
Cell 4 (row 2, column 1): roll - evasive forward roll, body tucked in a tight ball.
Cell 5 (row 2, column 2): blowback - powerful two-handed palm strike or spinning kick that blasts the opponent away to the right.
Cell 6 (row 2, column 3): super - Encore Fortissimo stance: dramatic super-move stance, both arms thrust forward to the right with compact energy, only a small glow at the hands.
Cell 7 (row 3, column 1): dizzy - dazed stagger, wobbly knees, hand on forehead.
Cell 8 (row 3, column 2): win2 - second celebratory victory pose, different from the first.
Cell 9 (row 3, column 3): lose - defeated, kneeling on one knee with the head bowed.
Flat uniform chroma green background RGB(0,255,0), no gradient, no floor shadow, no green on the subject, no lettering, borders, watermark, props outside the silhouette or detached debris. All clothing, shoes, soles, skin and accessories are fully opaque in their specified non-green colors: NO green apparel, green footwear, green reflections or translucent green body parts. Chroma green belongs only outside the character. Leave ample clear green padding around the whole subject. Use a solid clean ink silhouette, without a colored outline fringe. Accessories remain attached to the character; exactly one of each visible accessory.
